facts.statement: The genus Xiongguanlong was described by Li and colleagues in 2009.
facts.quote: authority: Li et al., 2009

facts.statement: Xiongguanlong lived during the Early Cretaceous period, between 124 and 113 million years ago.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Cretaceous~124 to 113 Ma -

facts.statement: The generic name Xiongguanlong combines the former name of Jiayuguan City, "Xiong Guan," meaning "grand pass," and the Mandarin word "long," meaning "dragon."
facts.quote: The generic name comes from Jiayuguan City (formerly called "Xiong Guan" or "grand pass") and the Mandarin word "long" which means dragon.

facts.statement: The species name baimoensis refers to the "White Ghost Castle," a geological feature at the fossil site.
facts.quote: The specific epithet, "baimoensis" is a latinization of the Mandarin word for "white ghost" in reference to one of the geological features of the type locality (nicknamed the "White Ghost Castle").

facts.statement: The fossils were found in the Xiagou Formation in the Yujingzi Basin of Gansu, China.
facts.quote: Xiongguanlong was discovered in the upper member of the Xiagou Formation of the Xinminbao Group at a locality nicknamed the "White Ghost Castle" which is in the Yujingzi Basin of Gansu, China.

facts.statement: Mark Norell, Peter Makovicky, and a team from Beijing University discovered and prepared the fossils between 2006 and 2007.
facts.quote: It was discovered in and prepared in 2006 and 2007 by Mark Norell, Peter Makovicky, and a team of scientists from Beijing University.

facts.statement: While initially hypothesized to be from the Aptian or Albian stages, later research constrained the age to the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: In their original description, the authors hypothesize that it is from either the Aptian or Albian stages, but subsequent authors have constrained the upper member to the Aptian stage specifically.

facts.statement: The single known specimen, designated FRDC-GS JB16-2-1, is housed at the Fossil Research and Development Center in Lanzhou, China.
facts.quote: The holotype, and only specimen, of Xiongguanlong was given the designation FRDC-GS JB16-2-1 and was deposited at the Fossil Research and Development Center of the Gansu Provincial Bureau of Geo-Exploration and Mineral Development in Lanzhou, China.

facts.statement: The holotype includes a complete skull without lower jaws, a full series of neck and back vertebrae, a partial right hip bone, and a right thigh bone.
facts.quote: It consists of a complete skull (lacking the lower jaws), a complete series of cervical and dorsal vertebrae, a partial right ilium, and the right femur.

facts.statement: Xiongguanlong is considered a significant transitional form between early Jurassic tyrannosauroids and late Cretaceous tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: In its initial description, and in numerous publications since, it has been remarked as a noteworthy transitional species between the basal tyrannosauroids of the Jurassic period and the derived tyrannosaurids of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Xiongguanlong is a basal tyrannosauroid that is more derived than Eotyrannus, positioning it closer to the Tyrannosauridae family.
facts.quote: While Xiongguanlong was a basal tyrannosauroid, it was more derived than forms like Eotyrannus, placing it closer to the origins of Tyrannosauridae.

facts.statement: Researchers estimated the length of Xiongguanlong to be approximately 5 meters.
facts.quote: The authors of its original description estimated that Xiongguanlong was about 5 m long.

facts.statement: Based on regression analysis, the estimated mass of Xiongguanlong is approximately 270 kilograms.
facts.quote: They used a regression analysis based on the work of P. Christiansen and R.A. Fariña to estimate its mass at approximately 270 kg.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Gregory S. Paul estimated the mass of Xiongguanlong to be about 200 kilograms.
facts.quote: However, Gregory S. Paul estimated that it only weighed about 200 kg.

facts.statement: Evidence of closed neurocentral sutures suggests the holotype specimen was fully grown.
facts.quote: The holotype is believed to have been completely or almost completely, fully-grown due to the observed closure of the neurocentral sutures.

facts.statement: Xiongguanlong's larger size compared to earlier tyrannosauroids like Dilong and Guanlong supports the idea that body size increased continuously during the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Its estimated size is much greater than earlier tyrannosauroids such as Dilong and Guanlong, which led the authors to suggest that body size increase in tyrannosauroids was a continuous process throughout the Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: The skull of Xiongguanlong is very elongated compared to other tyrannosauroids, particularly in the maxillary, lacrimal, and postorbital bones.
facts.quote: It is very elongated in comparison to most other tyrannosauroids, with significant elongation of the maxillary, lacrimal, and the postorbital bones.

facts.statement: Fused parietal bones feature a short, concave sagittal crest that served as an attachment point for bite muscles.
facts.quote: The parietal bones are fused and possess a short and concave sagittal crest, which served as attachment sites for the bite muscles.

facts.statement: Analysis of dental alveoli revealed that Xiongguanlong possessed four premaxillary teeth and fifteen maxillary teeth.
facts.quote: This led the authors of its description to determine that Xiongguanlong had four premaxillary teeth and fifteen maxillary teeth.

facts.statement: The maxillary teeth of Xiongguanlong are lateromedially narrow and blade-like, differing from those of more derived tyrannosauroids.
facts.quote: However, the maxillary teeth differ from more derived tyrannosauroids in being lateromedially narrow and more blade-like.

facts.statement: The neck vertebrae have centra that are strongly fused to the neural arches and are concave anteriorly and convex posteriorly.
facts.quote: The cervical centra are strongly co-ossified with the neural arches, and the centra are concave in anterior direction and convex in the posterior direction.

facts.statement: The cervical vertebrae possess pneumatic foramina, a feature not found in Albertosaurus, Daspletosaurus, or Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: They also possess a pair of pneumatic foramina on the vertebrae, which is unlike the condition seen in Albertosaurus, Daspletosaurus, and Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: The hip elements of Xiongguanlong resemble those of both derived tyrannosauroids and ornithomimosaurs.
facts.quote: The preserved hip elements of Xiongguanlong resemble those of derived tyrannosauroids as well as those of ornithomimosaurs.

facts.statement: A tibia found with the skeleton was likely not from the same animal due to its comparatively small size.
facts.quote: A tibia was also found with the rest of the skeleton, although its comparatively small size led Li and colleagues to conclude that it was probably not from the same animal as the rest of the bones.

facts.statement: Xiongguanlong was classified as a tyrannosauroid based on features including a vertical ridge on the ilium, a notch on the ilium's dorsal edge, fused nasal bones, and smaller premaxillary teeth compared to maxillary teeth.
facts.quote: a vertical ridge on the midline of the ilium, a notch on the dorsal edge of the ilium, fused nasal bones, and premaxillary teeth much smaller than the maxillary teeth

facts.statement: Xiongguanlong is considered a middle Cretaceous taxon that helps fill a gap in the fossil record of tyrannosauroids during that period.
facts.quote: The researchers who described the "middle Cretaceous" taxa including Xiongguanlong, Timurlengia, Moros, and Suskityrannus noted that these taxa partially fill this "Cretaceous tyrannosaur gap"

facts.statement: Evidence suggests some tyrannosauroids migrated to North America before 108 million years ago, a timeframe relevant to the era of Xiongguanlong.
facts.quote: Tyrannosauroid teeth are known from the Aptian-Albian aged Cloverly Formation of Wyoming, meaning that some tyrannosauroids had likely migrated to North America prior to 108 million years ago

facts.statement: The region where Xiongguanlong fossils were found was part of the Gobi Desert today but was likely near the coast of the Tethys Sea during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Today, this region is part of the Gobi Desert, but during the Early Cretaceous, it was a much less arid environment, and it was probably on or near the coast of the Tethys Sea

facts.statement: Xiongguanlong was the largest known predator found in the Xiagou Formation.
facts.quote: Xiongguanlong is the largest predator so-far discovered in the Xiagou Formation

facts.statement: Xiongguanlong was almost certainly an obligate carnivore, consistent with other known tyrannosauroids.
facts.quote: It was almost certainly an obligate carnivore, like all other known tyrannosauroids

facts.statement: Unlike derived tyrannosaurids, Xiongguanlong lacked adaptations for generating strong bite forces.
facts.quote: However, it did not possess the adaptations for strong bite forces that are characteristic of derived tyrannosaurids

facts.statement: Some authors debate whether the fossil record is sufficient to draw concrete conclusions about tyrannosauroid evolution and dispersal during the relevant Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: However, some authors believe that the fossil record from this part of the Cretaceous is too poor to make any concrete inferences as to the nature of tyrannosauroid evolution or dispersal

facts.statement: Xiongguanlong was a bipedal animal that balanced its body with a long tail, like most other theropods.
facts.quote: Xiongguanlong era un animal bípedo que equilibraba su cuerpo con una larga cola, como la mayoría de los otros terópodos.

facts.statement: Xiongguanlong was a small tyrannosauroid measuring 5 meters in length and weighing between 170 and 270 kilograms.
facts.quote: Era un tiranosauroide pequeño, que medía 5 metros de largo y pesaba entre 170 y 270 kilogramos

facts.statement: Its skull measured 50 centimeters in length and held 70 teeth that were less sharp than those of other tyrannosaurid species.
facts.quote: El cráneo medía 50 centímetros de largo y albergaba 70 dientes, escasamente afilados en comparación con otras especies de tiranosáuridos.

facts.statement: Unlike its relative Tyrannosaurus, Xiongguanlong had a longer and thinner snout adapted for cutting meat rather than crushing bones.
facts.quote: A diferencia de su pariente, Tyrannosaurus, el hocico es más alargado y fino que el de este, más adaptado a cortar carne que a triturar huesos.

facts.statement: Unlike Guanlong and other primitive tyrannosauroids, Xiongguanlong did not possess a crest on its snout.
facts.quote: A diferencia del Guanlong y otros tiranosauroides primitivos no poseía una cresta sobre el hocico.

facts.statement: Peter Makovicky noted that the fossils show distinct traits of Tyrannosaurus rex, including a box-shaped skull, reinforced cheekbones to support jaw muscles, and a strong spine supporting a large head.
facts.quote: Peter Makovicky explicó en la revista Proceedings de la Royal Society británica que en esos restos ya se aprecian algunos rasgos distintivos del Tyrannosaurus rex, un cráneo en forma de caja, huesos reforzados en la sien para soportar la musculatura maxilar y una fuerte columna vertebral que sostiene una gran cabeza.

facts.statement: Xiongguanlong fossils were found in Jiayuguan city, Gansu province, in the Xinminpu Group in western China.
facts.quote: Xiongguanlong se basa en unos fósiles encontrados en la ciudad de Jiayuguan, provincia de Gansu en el Grupo Xinminpu al oeste de la China.

facts.statement: The type species X. baimoensis was described online in 2009 by a team of researchers from China and the United States and formally published in January 2009.
facts.quote: La especie tipo es X. baimoensis, fue descrita en línea en 2009 por un grupo de investigadores de China y Estados Unidos y publicada formalmente en enero de 2009.

facts.statement: The fossils include a skull, vertebrae, a right ilium, and a right femur.
facts.quote: Los fósiles incluyen un cráneo ,vértebras , un ilion derecho y el fémur derecho.

facts.statement: The fossils were found in rocks from the Xiagou Formation, which preserves fossils from the late Aptian.
facts.quote: Las rocas en las que se encontró son de la Formación Xiagou, que conserva fósiles de finales del Aptiense.

facts.statement: The generic name derives from the Chinese term xiong guan (Jiayuguan, great pass) and long (dragon), while the specific name comes from baimo (white ghost), referring to the discovery area known as the White Ghost Castle in the southern Gobi Desert.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico deriva del término chino xiong guan, Jiayuguan, gran paso, y long, dragón, mientras que el específico viene de baimo o fantasma blanco, por el área del descubrimiento, conocida como el castillo del fantasma blanco, sur del desierto del Gobi.

facts.statement: Xiongguanlong lived during the mid-Cretaceous period, approximately between 123 and 113 million years ago, from the Aptian to the Albian stages, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 123 y 113 millones de años, desde el Aptiense al Albiense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: The time range for Xiongguanlong is the Aptian stage, from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: In the phylogenetic analysis proposed by the authors, Xiongguanlong appears as a sister taxon to Tyrannosauridae and Appalachiosaurus.
facts.quote: Xiongguanlong aparece en el análisis filogenético propuesto por los autores como un taxón hermano a Tyrannosauridae más Appalachiosaurus

facts.statement: It has been found that Xiongguanlong is closely related to Alectrosaurus.
facts.quote: Se ha encontrado que está estrechamente relacionado con Alectrosaurus.

facts.statement: Body mass estimates for the mature Xiongguanlong specimen fall between those of late Cretaceous tyrannosaurs and Barremian tyrannosaurs, suggesting the trend of increasing body size in North American Tyrannosauridae may extend earlier in the clade's history, though phylogenetic work is required to corroborate this.
facts.quote: Las estimaciones de la masa del cuerpo para el espécimen maduro de Xiongguanlong está entre las de últimos tiranosáuridos cretáceos y los tiranosáuridos del Barremiano, sugiriendo que la tendencia del tamaño de cuerpo cada vez mayor observado en los Tyrannosauridae norteamericanos de finales de la era de los dinosaurios, puede extenderse antes en la historia del clado, sin embargo trabajos filogenéticos se requieren corroborar esto.

facts.statement: The thin, crestless nasals of Xiongguanlong contradict the recent hypothesis of correlated progression in tyrannosaurid feeding mechanics and suggest more complex patterns of character evolution in the integration of feeding adaptations in tyrannosaurs.
facts.quote: Los nasales delgados, sin cresta de Xiongguanlong contrarían con la reciente hipótesis de la progresión correlacionada en mecánicos de alimentación del tiranosáuridos, y sugieren patrones más complejos de la evolución del carácter en la integración de adaptaciones de alimentación en tiranosáuridos.

facts.statement: The vertebrae were more robust than in other basal tyrannosauroids, possibly to better support a large skull with a long snout similar to that of Alioramus.
facts.quote: Las vértebras eran más robustas que en otros tiranosauroides basales , posiblemente para soportar mejor un cráneo grande que tenía un hocico largo parecido al de Alioramus.
